author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-11-11 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Once out of my skull, an unearthly wind caused my head – as well as the house – to rattle.
context_before: me life was the cause of my breathing and consciousness. I thought my physical body was me, not realizing it was simply where the real me was buried.
context_after: Looking for the cause, my attention was diverted for a few seconds. And when I looked back, my body was gone and in its place were my three brothers. One was sitting where the head had been, while the other two were sitting at the feet. Disturbed by the sound, one rose and moved in the direction of the wind. Looking down, he said: “Why, it’s Neville’s baby.” The other two questioned his words, saying: “How can Neville have a baby?” Without arguing the point, my brother reached down, picked up a baby wrapped in swaddling clothes, and placed it on the bed. Then I, as though having rehearsed the drama in eternity, took the babe in my arms and said: “How is my sweetheart?” as the child broke into a heavenly smile. Then the scene dissolved and I awoke.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).
